utility.notes: SMUD is a municipal (publicly-owned) electric utility. Multiple corroborating sources confirm SMUD serves Folsom, including SMUD's own community outreach events (an annual 'Folsom Electricity Fair') and a new SMUD operations center under construction in Folsom.

value.name: Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD)
value.notes: SMUD is a vertically-integrated municipal utility — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA, consistent with the pattern already established for the City of Sacramento and Elk Grove this session.

value.name: My Energy Optimizer Partner+
value.description: SMUD's own battery storage incentive program (separate from the CPUC/IOU-administered SGIP, which does not apply to SMUD customers as a municipal utility outside CPUC jurisdiction). One-time enrollment incentive of up to $10,000 per household ($500/kWh minus a 20% holdback) for new battery energy storage system customers who enroll within 90 days of receiving Permission to Operate (PTO) from SMUD. Ongoing quarterly incentives are currently only available for Tesla batteries ($110 for 1 battery, $220 for 2, $330 for 3+); other eligible brands (Eguana, Enphase, Franklin, SolarEdge, Sonnen) receive only the one-time enrollment incentive at this time.
value.eligibility: SMUD residential customers with a battery storage unit installed at their home who participate in SMUD's Solar and Storage Rate (SSR). Individual rental units are currently ineligible; multifamily homes are eligible with the same tenant restrictions. MED Rate customers are not eligible.

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Instant Solar Permitting' page: applicants upload these into Symbium as part of the application; project plans are listed as optional.

inspection_steps.notes: The City's page describes the Symbium/eTRAKiT application and fee-payment workflow and states an 'Inspection Checklist' is downloadable after permit issuance, but does not itself detail how to schedule or request the physical inspection.

value.notes: The City's own page states: 'automated plan review with approvals issued in as little as 24 business hours for eligible projects.' Recorded as 0-3 calendar days to conservatively bound '24 business hours' (roughly 3 business days at a standard 8-hour business day) without asserting same-day issuance as guaranteed.

eligibility_constraints.notes: The City's page refers to 'eligible projects' for the 24-business-hour approval figure but does not itself state the specific eligibility criteria (system size, property type, etc.).
